SMTO-GML-0072 — SMTO stopped to avoid doing the same email action twice

GUID: f736f589-7c0a-40e2-a7fa-3f090c6e1fc2
Slug: gmail-compound-replay-blocked
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-client-actions

What happened

  • Earlier in this Task, SMTO already started this same reply, email import or filter. Doing it again could send a second reply, import a duplicate email or make a second filter, so SMTO stopped. The earlier attempt may have worked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether the earlier action already happened: look in Gmail's Sent folder for the reply, in your mailbox for the imported email, or in Gmail's filter settings for the filter. SMTO stopped because the first attempt may already have done the work.
  2. If the reply was sent but the email wasn't archived, ask SMTO only to archive that conversation. A problem with archiving doesn't mean the reply failed, and asking to reply again could send a second copy.
  3. Only if you've confirmed it didn't happen, send SMTO a new message asking for that one action again. Within this same Task, SMTO keeps refusing to repeat that action to protect you from duplicates.

What success looks like

  • Gmail shows exactly one copy of the reply, imported email or filter, and anything left over, such as archiving, is done.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking SMTO to resend the reply; check Gmail's Sent folder first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • guard_effect found another invocation in this run that already reserved the same send, import or filter-creation effect digest, and raised gmail_compound_replay_blocked naming that earlier operation.

What this means

  • The existing run receipt holds a semantic effect digest. A new tool-call ID cannot bypass this reservation, even when a later archive or cleanup failed or the controller restarted.

Why this can happen

  • The existing run receipt holds a semantic effect digest. A new tool-call ID cannot bypass this reservation, even when a later archive or cleanup failed or the controller restarted.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected account, action arguments and operation reference; do not infer mailbox effects from the error alone.

How to fix it

  • Read the receipt of the operation_ref named in the error and confirm the earlier effect in Gmail (Sent message, imported message ID, or filter list). If the send succeeded, request only the remaining archive; if the earlier effect is uncertain, inspect it before any further write. A new tool-call ID cannot clear the reservation, and an archive or cleanup failure never authorizes another send.
  • Read the referenced operation receipt. If sending succeeded, request only the remaining archive; if an effect is uncertain, inspect it before further writes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the referenced operation receipt. If sending succeeded, request only the remaining archive; if an effect is uncertain, inspect it before further writes.

How to verify the fix

  • The saved confirmed effect remains single and follow-up work addresses only the remaining step.

What not to do

  • Do not interpret an archive failure as permission to send again.

Technical notes

  • Previously acknowledged changes remain confirmed; missing acknowledgments remain unknown. No automatic replay is authorized.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
